newsitem.title: UK: Northern takeover probe seen going into '97.
newsitem.headline: Northern takeover probe seen going into '97.

text.p: An investigation into British utility Northern Electric's defence against CE Electric's hostile bid is likely to last into the new year, a spokesman for the main target of the investigation said on Monday.
"I would think so, yes," said Peter Baillie a spokesman for investment bank BZW, when asked.

British watchdog The Takeover Panel said on Monday that it was investigating the circumstances under which it received information from Northern's advisers during the 782 million stg ($1.3 billion) bid by CE Electric.

The role of Northern's adviser, investment bank BZW, has been under scrutiny since it failed to disclose until last Friday a 250,000 stg payment from Northern for its services, in addition to its 1.5 million stg fixed fee.
BZW has denied any wrongdoing. The spokesman told Reuters: "We have absolutely nothing to hide from an investigation and we expect to be fully exonerated."
The decision to investigate the bid came hot on the heels of of a Panel move on Friday to extend the bid timetable to 1300 GMT on Tuesday for unspecified reasons.

The Takeover Panel has so far declined to say what effect the investigation might or might not have on the extension of the offer to December 24 -- and whether or not the share acceptances received by CE Electric since Friday are valid.

Northern's independence has been on a knife-edge since last Friday, when the bid timetable ticked to a close and CE Electric, which is controlled by energy utility CalEnergy, fell fractionally short of winning control.
However, CE Electric had by Monday boosted shareholder acceptances for its bid to just over the 50 percent needed for victory -- from 49.77 percent on Friday.
Consequently, Northern Electric earlier on Monday launched an appeal of the decision to extend the bid deadline and requested that its shares be temporarily suspended.
